districtFact: Akron's calendar does not use one permanent opening pattern. For 2026–27, the one-page PDF lists August 27 as the student start, while the live district calendar specifies grades 1–12 on August 27, kindergarten phase-in August 27–28, and Pre-K and kindergarten on August 31.
profileDisclaimer: The district's Schools page describes 47 schools or Community Learning Centers and a student body of more than 21,000. School and enrollment figures can change as facilities and programs are reorganized.

about.title: Start Dates Vary by School Year
about.content: In 2025–26, grades 1–12 started August 21, kindergarten used appointment and phase-in dates, and Pre-K and kindergarten began together August 25. For 2026–27, grades 1–12 start August 27, kindergarten phases in August 27–28, and Pre-K and kindergarten begin August 31.

about.title: No Students Does Not Always Mean Offices Are Closed
about.content: APS distinguishes staff and conference days when students stay home from holidays when schools and district offices close. During longer breaks, check whether the calendar closes schools only or both schools and district offices.

about.title: Akron Schools Double as Community Learning Centers
about.content: APS calls most campuses Community Learning Centers, or CLCs. The district says these buildings are co-owned with the City of Akron and support community activities after the school day, making building availability broader than the student attendance calendar alone.

about.title: A Citywide Rebuilding Program Shapes the Campus Network
about.content: The official Schools page describes an approximately $800 million effort that rebuilt all but a handful of campuses as modern, technology-ready and energy-efficient facilities. Families will see CLC in many elementary, middle and high school names.

about.title: College and Career Academies Add Program-Level Planning
about.content: APS lists 15 academies and 54 college and career pathways for middle- and high-school students, supported by business and community partners. Academy showcases, internships and pathway events belong on the student's program calendar even when they are absent from the district attendance sheet.

about.title: Specialty Options Extend Beyond Neighborhood Campuses
about.content: Official offerings include Akron Early College, Firestone's International Baccalaureate and arts programs, NIHF STEM middle and high schools, and Miller South visual and performing arts. Their admissions and program events require a second calendar check.

calendarNotes: Use the APS annual calendar as the districtwide attendance baseline, then check the live calendar for grade and program details. The 2025–26 page separates grades 1–12, kindergarten appointments and phase-in, and the first full Pre-K/kindergarten day. For 2026–27, the PDF gives a general August 27 student start while the live calendar adds grades 1–12, kindergarten phase-in, and the August 31 Pre-K/kindergarten start. Staff professional-development, teacher work, records, and conference days mean no students but do not automatically close district offices. Holidays labeled schools and offices closed affect both. CLC activities, academy events, specialty-program deadlines, athletics, transportation changes, and emergency closures may appear only on school or program calendars.

planningTips.title: Planning with the Akron APS Calendar
content: Check the student's grade or program before saving a first day; APS uses grade-specific openings and kindergarten phase-in dates.
For 2025–26 kindergarten, keep the school's August 21 or 22 appointment and phase-in instructions separate from the August 25 first full program day.
Reserve childcare for staff development, records and conference days even when APS offices remain open.
During Thanksgiving and Winter Break, read the office-status note before assuming the central office is closed for the full student break.
For a senior in 2025–26, use the grade 12 final day rather than the later districtwide student ending.
Pair this calendar with the assigned CLC, College and Career Academy, early-college, STEM, arts, IB or alternative-program calendar.
Treat an imported ICS file as a snapshot and recheck APS for weather, emergency, transportation and building-level updates.

districtFaqs.q: Do all Akron Public Schools students start on the same day?
districtFaqs.a: No. For 2026–27, grades 1–12 start August 27, kindergarten phases in August 27–28, and Pre-K and kindergarten begin August 31. Other school years use their own grade-specific dates.

districtFaqs.q: What does CLC mean in Akron Public Schools?
districtFaqs.a: CLC means Community Learning Center. APS says the City of Akron and the school district co-own these campuses, which also host community activities after the school day.

districtFaqs.q: Are APS offices closed every time students have no school?
districtFaqs.a: No. Staff development, records and conference dates are labeled no-student days, while only specific holidays say schools and offices are closed. Longer breaks also identify selected office-closure dates.

districtFaqs.q: Did Akron seniors finish before other students in 2025–26?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. The official page lists May 22, 2026 as the final day for grade 12 and May 28 as the final day for students generally.

districtFaqs.q: Does APS publish a PDF for both reviewed years?
districtFaqs.a: No. The official 2025–26 source is a web page of holidays and breaks. APS publishes the reviewed 2026–27 calendar as a one-page PDF from its district calendar hub.

districtFaqs.q: Do APS specialty programs have additional dates?
districtFaqs.a: They can. Early College, STEM, arts, IB, academy and alternative programs may publish admissions, orientation, pathway, testing or campus events beyond the district attendance calendar.
